**Did fitting in normalized units help? Most clearly for direct PSD.**
It removed all observed unit-dependent success/failure differences and improved
equality-constrained fitting. Ordinary ML changed little. The two-stage route
still has failures; this run does not settle whether it should replace direct PSD.

## The important numbers

Each cell shows **successful cases before → after normalization**. Both arms
use the same current accuracy checks. Direct PSD fits under PSD restrictions
from the start; two-stage first tries ordinary ML and uses PSD when needed.

```{r}
x <- read.csv("results/normalization-revisit/paired/family.csv")
order <- c("constrained", "boomsma", "chen", "engineering15", "research47", "wolf")
labels <- c("Equalities", "Boomsma", "Chen", "Engineering stress cases", "Research stress cases", "Wolf")
a <- x[x$arm == "original_units", ]; b <- x[x$arm == "normalized", ]
p <- merge(a, b, by=c("family", "route"), suffixes=c("_before", "_after"))
t <- data.frame(Family=labels, Cases=a$attempts[match(order, a$family)])
for (route in c("ml", "direct", "two_stage")) {
  z <- p[p$route == route, ]; z <- z[match(order, z$family), ]
  t[[switch(route, ml="ML", direct="Direct PSD", two_stage="Two-stage PSD")]] <-
    paste0(z$success_before, " → ", z$success_after)
}
knitr::kable(t, row.names=FALSE, align=c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r"))
```

**What are the 180 equality cases?** Five populations × two model variants ×
two sample sizes × three simulated samples × three unit scales. That is
**30 independent datasets**, reused across models and scales—not 180 independent
datasets. Across all families there are 1,356 cases, each fitted six ways:
three methods, with normalization off/on (8,136 fits).

“Success” means the library certifies convergence; PSD routes also require its
admissibility verdict. ML may have negative variances, so its successes do not
mean the same thing as PSD successes.

## What changed—and what remains

- **More consistent across units.** Among 1,002 comparisons with rescaled data,
  direct PSD's success/failure disagreements fell **18 → 0**; objective and
  fitted-covariance disagreements also disappeared among jointly successful
  fits. Two-stage verdict disagreements fell **19 → 4**; ML rose **1 → 4**.
- **Most apparent two-stage objective losses were misleading.** Of 25 cases
  with a higher objective after normalization, **23 old accepted solutions
  actually violated PSD**. Normalized fitting rejected those ordinary solutions
  and proceeded to PSD. Two unexplained objective losses remain, plus one for
  direct PSD.
- **Normalization is not a universal convergence fix.** Direct PSD gained 16
  successes but lost six; ML gained two and lost five; two-stage gained eleven
  and lost eleven. All losses are saved for investigation.

**Next:** investigate constrained PSD finalization failures and make
admissibility checks reliable under mixed variable scales. Barrier normalization
remains the first implementation TODO. No new route choice is justified yet.

**Scope:** saved development cases, only three samples per sample size, with
repeated unit versions. Means and linear equalities are included; groups and
barrier are not tested here. These results do not establish performance on fresh
held-out problems.
